pr_title: Add ui.EDITOR_EOL, default to saving files with LF again
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/28097
Replaces: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/28101

Assuming we consider it a bug that people on Windows get CRLF endings without a editorconfig, we should backport this to 1.21.
pr_comments:
I do not think this is right.

See the discussion https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/27141#discussion_r1331139585

Even if you set `model.setEOL(monaco.editor.EndOfLineSequence.LF);`, you still get `\r\n` when submitting the form

![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/2114189/843edfab-16a3-4e27-9a15-77d35530335a)


I believe the best choice is to revert #27141 at the moment, make 1.21 users happy. At least, "\n" is more widely used but "\r\n" causes problems in POSIX.
If that's because of textarea behaviour, we can fix this by setting the textarea value.

Added the previous server-side eol convertion back, but it now respects the new setting of LF vs. CRLF too: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/28119/commits/e58dcc03437dca23ed8bc24c8b7434ac088e14be
I guess the only thing missing here is to respect editorconfig on server-side as well, but for all intends, this will restore the previous replacement to LF that was done server-side.

> I guess the only thing missing here is to respect editorconfig on server-side as well, but for all intends, this will restore the previous replacement to LF that was done server-side.

Done as well in https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/28119/commits/2dfcfe005020976842014e33586331639bed42e5, now the server also respects the editorconfig for this replacement. I guess it's still good to retain the client-side stuff so that copy out of monaco copies with the correct line endings.

* If there is no "editorconfig", it should use the original EOL. eg: if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"; if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"
* The config option "EDITOR_EOL" is not necessary (not used in most cases, according to the behavior above), the newly created file could just use "
", which is widely used and doesn't cause problem in modern days.
* I guess the JS trick for `data-initial-value="{{JsonUtils.EncodeToString .FileContent}}"` is a no-op now, it should work well by using `<textarea>{{.FileContent}}</textarea>` ?

> * If there is no "editorconfig", it should use the original EOL. eg: if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"; if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"

The same problem as BOM: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/28935#issuecomment-1912115491 

* if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"; if the file was stored in "
", the newly saved file should also use "
"
* (and more) if the file was stored with some BOM, the newly saved file should also use that BOM

> if the file was stored in "\n", the newly saved file should also use "\n"; if the file was stored in "\r\n", the newly saved file should also use "\r\n"

Yes, like with BOM we should just round-trip the file unmodified. The only problem is new files and files with equal amount of CRLF and LF, for those we need to bias towards one format, which could come from editorconfig with fallback to global server config.

I think the approach here is not correct and we should actually avoid backend convertion completely. So I think it's better to make a new PR, maybe I will have a look later, but feel free to raise something @wxiaoguang.

> I think the approach here is not correct and we should actually avoid backend convertion completely.

IMO at the moment, backend convertion can't be avoided. Because HTML textarea **always** passes "\r\n" to backend, it is the standard.

> > I think the approach here is not correct and we should actually avoid backend convertion completely.
> 
> IMO at the moment, backend convertion can't be avoided. Because HTML textarea **always** passes "\r\n" to backend, it is the standard.

Yeah, but we can at least avoid altering the content until the point where it reaches the editor. Maybe it's ideal to use a `data-` attribute to ensure the browser does no shenenigans with the textarea value even when reading it.

issue_context.title: 1.21 broke Linux EOL in code editor
issue_context.body:
### Description

Updated to 1.21 and now any change via web editor always use Windows EOL, quite possibly because the browser itself runs in a Windows PC.

The stupid part is the editor itself successfully detected these are bash scripts, which must be Linux!
I can't find any documentation on how to permanently use Linux EOL so now I'm stuck.

Tried revert back to 1.20 and of course gitea blocked it too.

### Gitea Version

1.21

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Git Version

_No response_

### Operating System

_No response_

### How are you running Gitea?

Gitea docker on Ubuntu.
Browser access on Windows PC.

### Database

None
comments:
> any change via web editor always use Windows EOL, quite possibly because the browser itself runs in a Windows PC.

That should not be the behaviour I tested. Do you have a `.editorconfig` file in the repo? If not, it should use LF already, the browser OS is not part of the detection in the Monaco editor, as far as I'm aware. It should give you LF when no .editorconfig is present.

As per my current understanding, the only way you get CRLF is when you have a .editorconfig specifying CRLF for the file or when the file is already predominantly in CRLF. All other cases should get you LF.

@testdasi please let me know what [this](https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/playground.html?source=v0.44.0#XQAAAAIUAQAAAAAAAABBqQkHQ5NjdMjwa-jY7SIQ9S7DNlzs5W-mwj0fe1ZCDRFc9ws9XQE0SJE1jc2VKxhaLFIw9vEWSxW3yscpr6MsNg4vHoYKiujoNF7STKsikuAnq3yOVCHCMPueylLD-VoHOlF3w7elBXLBzOq_Ka4_q7xdHjgZ816TR650ms14N1DvUJ2VMmrE3JxsFVAsJ10g4GoLDneKIarapH9FeS22-0LgGuPBqc3r1bW7Od_iiAuh-FUMe9Z2G5BzBa5XwOHj9peFGELupDprrG1qY93NKtI4K6VZhrmmh8QpXP6vk2o) displays on your affected machine:

It's "\r\n" for both Chrome, Firefox, Edge. Even when I spoofed my User Agent as a Mac Firefox. :(
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/51292604/e191a2ad-3384-4bdf-9f22-aba923484058)
Interesting, so Monaco seems to use OS defaults for files without a dominant ending. I think we should default it to `\n` but have a config option in case someone wants to change this default.

By the way, where does this case conversation happen? It's not from the ini package, right?

Or how do we want to handle this case?
I can live both with the current approach of removing it completely, and my proposed approach of only converting `\r\n -> \n`
